correctness.rationale: For protected vertex v, failure means all neighbors of v fail and the remaining survivors form an independent set. Therefore 1-R_v=q^(n-1)I(T-N[v];p/q); the factor q^(n-1) is common. Independent fresh exhaustive Prüfer enumeration of every labeled tree of size 2..7, with direct independent-set subset counts, gave per-size (total, nondominance) (1,0),(3,0),(16,0),(125,0),(1296,0),(16807,840). Every one of the 840 nondominance cases has precisely the equally subdivided 3-star structure (automorphism group size 6). Its center residual polynomial is (1+t)^3 and arm-neighbor residual polynomial is (1+2t)^2, with leaf residual polynomial 1+5t+6t²+t³. Center-minus-arm success is p(1-p)^3(1-p-p²), giving the unique golden threshold. All n<=7 are exhausted, not sampled; no assertion above n=7.
residual_risks: Finite exhaustive classification is only for orders two through seven, and does not assert a universal bound above seven.

final_claim: For a finite tree of order 2 through 6, independent identical survival with one permanently protected vertex admits a protected vertex maximizing the probability of at least one surviving edge for all 0<p<1. At order 7, the only counterexample up to isomorphism is the equally subdivided three-arm star; the center-versus-arm optimum changes uniquely at p=(sqrt(5)-1)/2.
limitations: Finite exhaustive classification is only for orders two through seven, and does not assert a universal bound above seven.
